blind_spots.blind_spot: The whole architecture bets on a low-latency link between the headset and a cloud/on-prem render farm, in exactly the buildings that will not provide one
blind_spots.operator_reality: Depot maintenance bays, paint hangars and flight lines are metal, RF-hostile and often shielded; base networks are congested NIPRNet with GovCloud round trips measured in hundreds of milliseconds. A HoloLens waiting on a streamed high-polygon mesh over that path shows the artisan a frozen overlay on a live aircraft. This is the 30fps crowd-detection failure mode with meshes instead of frames — the fix is decoupling fidelity from the link (local cached LOD, deltas only), and it has to be designed in before the STRATFI period ends, not after the first hangar trial.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The platform's entire differentiation is that rendering happens off-device — the company has explicitly argued the edge device cannot do it, so the connectivity assumption is load-bearing to the product story and cannot be questioned from inside.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: These levels of visual fidelity and performance are impossible to achieve when processing models on the edge device itself.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Ingesting weapon-system technical data while running an engineering office in India, with no ITAR or 800-171/CMMC language anywhere
blind_spots.operator_reality: HIMARS paint-masking geometry and WR-ALC PLM/CAD data are ITAR-controlled technical data. Access by foreign persons — including their own engineers in Bengaluru — is an export event, and the government's flow-down requires NIST 800-171/CMMC on the systems that hold it. A program office or DCMA review stops the transition on the compliance package long before the technology is the issue, and the remediation (segregated US-person enclave, access controls, a documented technology control plan) takes months the period of performance does not have.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's core identity is industrial/commercial spatial computing where global engineering is a cost advantage; the defense work arrived as projects on top of that org chart, so nobody re-architected data residency for controlled technical data.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: INDIA OFFICE:#5, 3rd Floor, 9th Main Road, 5th Block, Jayanagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka – 560041, India

blind_spots.blind_spot: The delivery device is a head-mounted display, with no sustainment, training or device-logistics story for the person wearing it all shift
blind_spots.operator_reality: A depot artisan works in gloves, safety glasses and — in a paint booth — a respirator, for eight hours. HoloLens and Vision Pro do not survive that: battery swaps, hygiene, prescription/PPE eyewear conflicts, drop damage, and a spares pipeline nobody has funded. Adoption is decided by the shop chief who has to staff and sustain it, not by the engineer who demos it for twenty minutes, and there is no advocacy chain above that shop chief in anything they publish.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their proof points are technology awards and manufacturing-innovation prizes, which are won on capability demonstrations; nothing in that feedback loop rewards thinking about spares, PPE compatibility or who trains the second shift.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Supports Apple Vision Pro, iOS, Microsoft HoloLens, Android XR

opener_hook: GridRaster's platform page states that this level of fidelity is 'impossible to achieve when processing models on the edge device itself' — which makes the depot network, not the AI, the thing that decides whether the WR-ALC paint-masking work becomes a fielded capability.
what_they_do: Cloud/edge-streamed spatial AI and XR platform (SPIDER) that builds digital twins and guides inspection, maintenance and paint masking for aerospace and defense depots.
